title: The 10 Best Blenders for Smoothies
metaDescription: Our 10 picks for blenders for smoothies, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at blenders for smoothies using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: NutriBullet 600W Compact Personal Blender
products.blurb: Key specs: 600W motor, 24-oz blending cup, Cyclonic extractor blade.
strengths: Blends and drinks from the same 24-oz cup, cutting cleanup to a rinse
600W is enough for softened or lightly frozen fruit without stalling
Compact footprint fits on crowded counters and travels in a bag
Replacement cups, blades, and gaskets are cheap and widely available
limitations: 600W bogs down on fully frozen fruit straight from the freezer without a short thaw
Not rated for crushing dry ice cubes
24-oz cup caps out at a single serving
No speed control, one button, one speed
features: Blends and drinks from same cup

products.name: Ninja Professional Plus Blender BN701 72-oz
products.blurb: Key specs: 1,000W motor, 72-oz Tritan container, Total Crushing stacked blade assembly.
strengths: Stacked blade design contacts frozen fruit and greens at multiple heights, producing smooth results in 30 to 45 seconds
72-oz container batches 4 to 6 servings in one blend
Auto-iQ programs remove the guesswork on blend timing
Certified to crush ice cubes without added liquid
limitations: Leaves detectable chunks in raw kale stems or fully frozen mango where a Vitamix does not
No variable speed dial, three fixed speeds plus pulse
No tamper included for pushing dense blends toward the blade
1-year warranty versus 5 to 7 years on Vitamix models

products.name: Vitamix E310 Explorian Blender 48-oz
products.blurb: Key specs: 1,490W motor, 48-oz Tritan container, Hammerhead blade geometry (same as the 5200).
strengths: Same blade geometry and motor class as the flagship 5200 at a lower entry price
Silky results on raw kale stems, fresh ginger, and dense frozen combinations that chunk in a Ninja
10-speed dial gives precise control over texture, from chunky to fully smooth
Self-cleans in 30 to 60 seconds with warm water and soap
5-year warranty and a documented multi-decade household lifespan
limitations: 48-oz container is smaller than the 5200's 64-oz jar for large batches
No preset programs, manual dial and pulse only
Loud at high speed, in the high-80s dB range

products.name: NutriBullet Pro 900 Personal Blender
products.blurb: Key specs: 900W motor, 32-oz colossal cup, Cyclonic extractor blade.
strengths: 900W handles fully frozen fruit and leafy greens that stall the 600W model
32-oz cup covers a bigger single serving or a light second portion
Extractor blade design pulls seeds and stems into the cutting zone more completely than a flat blade
Replacement gaskets and blades are widely stocked, extending the cup's useful life
limitations: Louder than the 600W model at comparable size
Cup seal gasket is the first part to wear and needs periodic replacement
No speed control, single-speed motor like other NutriBullet models
features: Blends and drinks from same cup

products.name: Oster Pro 1200 Blender 6-Cup
products.blurb: Key specs: 1,200W motor, 6-cup (48-oz) glass jar, 7-speed dial plus pulse.
strengths: 1,200W is more power than most blenders at this price, enough for daily frozen fruit and ice
Glass jar resists scratching and clouding better than plastic containers over years of use
7-speed dial gives more granular control than typical budget blenders' 2 to 3 speeds
limitations: Motor strains on fully frozen, low-liquid blends more than the Ninja or Vitamix
Glass jar is heavier and more prone to chipping than Tritan plastic
Toggle switches feel less durable than dial or touch controls over years of daily use
1-year warranty and a shorter documented lifespan than premium options

products.name: Ninja BL770 Mega Kitchen System 72-oz
products.blurb: Key specs: 1,500W motor, 72-oz pitcher plus 16-oz personal cup, Total Crushing stacked blade system.
strengths: 1,500W and a 72-oz pitcher batch enough smoothie for a family of 4 in one run
Comes with a personal cup, covering both batch and single-serve needs without buying two machines
Stacked blade system produces smoother results on leafy greens than single-tier competitors
limitations: Larger footprint takes up more counter and cabinet space than a standard pitcher blender
1-year warranty despite the higher price point
Multiple accessories (pitcher, cup, blades) mean more parts to track and clean

products.name: Vitamix 5200 Blender Professional-Grade 64-oz
products.blurb: Key specs: 2-peak HP motor (~1380W), 64-oz Tritan jar, Fixed hammerhead blade assembly.
strengths: Processes fibrous greens and dense frozen combinations to fully smooth in one 45 to 60-second cycle
64-oz jar handles family-size batches without a second blend cycle
7-year warranty and a documented 15+ year household lifespan
Self-cleans in 60 seconds, faster than disassembling a removable-blade blender
limitations: 17.5-inch height with jar does not clear most under-cabinet spaces
88 to 95 dB at high speed, loud enough to interrupt nearby conversation
No preset programs, manual dial only on the 5200

products.name: Ninja SS201 Foodi Power Nutri 72-oz Blender
products.blurb: Key specs: 1,400W motor, 72-oz pitcher, Nutri Ninja cups included.
strengths: 1,400W handles frozen fruit and ice without straining
Combo cup system lets one motor base run both pitcher and personal-cup blends
Auto-iQ smoothie preset produces consistent results without manual timing
72-oz pitcher covers multi-serving batches on the same base as the single-serve cups
limitations: More parts (pitcher, cups, blade assemblies) to store and keep track of than a single-format blender
Motor overheats on sustained heavy loads like nut butter
1-year warranty, shorter than premium countertop options
features: Auto-iQ Smoothie and Frozen Drink presets
Blade-lock cup adapter for single-serve blending

products.name: Breville Super Q Personal Blender BBL920BTR
products.blurb: Key specs: 1,000W+ motor, Noise-dampening acoustic housing, Personal-size blending cup.
strengths: Acoustic dampening housing brings noise down to roughly 65 to 75 dB, noticeably quieter than a Ninja or Vitamix at similar power
Digital presets remove guesswork from single-serve smoothie timing
Strong enough motor to handle frozen fruit without the muted sound suggesting reduced power
5-year warranty is longer than most personal blenders offer
limitations: Higher price than comparable non-dampened personal blenders
Single-serve cup size limits batch blending for multiple people

products.name: KitchenAid KSB4027CU K400 Blender 56-oz
products.blurb: Key specs: 1.5-peak HP motor, 56-oz BPA-free pitcher, 5 pre-programmed settings including Smoothie and Ice Crush.
strengths: Intelli-Speed control senses blend thickness and adjusts motor speed automatically, reducing manual monitoring
56-oz pitcher fits 2 to 4 smoothie servings per blend
5 preset programs cover most household use cases without manual dialing
Distinct, appliance-matching design for kitchens already built around KitchenAid
limitations: 1.5-peak HP trails the Vitamix and top Ninja models on dense or fibrous blends
Higher price than Ninja options with comparable smoothie performance
features: 5 pre-programmed settings including Smoothie and Ice Crush
Intelli-Speed motor control adjusts speed automatically during blend

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
We do not list prices or star ratings because they change. Check Amazon for current details.
